supervisor.summary: After round 1's fact corrections the five forecasts converged tightly: fair values $83-86, ladder medians ~$83-85, all using $4.58 FY28 consensus, ~7.5-8% tax, 575M shares and ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt. The main risk is an upcycle that peaks around mid-2027, just before the horizon, together with high rates capping semis multiples. The next checkpoint is Q2 FY27 results around early November.

fair_value.reason: P/E: 18.5-19x NTM EPS of ~$4.55-4.65 at Sep-2027 (575M shares, ~8% tax, light haircut to consensus) = ~$86. FCF yield (equity basis, FCF after interest and before the ~$111M preferred dividend, over 575M as-converted shares): ~$2.45-2.6B FY28 FCF at a 5.0-5.2% required yield = $85.2-87.0 (2.45/0.05/0.575; 2.6/0.052/0.575), no net-debt deduction because FCF is already after interest. EV/EBITDA: harmonized at ~16x on ~$3.2B EBITDA, less $3.8B net debt, = ~$82, instead of the agents' 14-15x ($73-78), which double-counts the derating already in the P/E multiple. Weighted about 0.5/0.3/0.2, that gives ~$85, slightly above the $84.3 forecaster mean.

supervisor_round1.summary: The five forecasts agree closely (fair values $82-87, medians ~$81-84). Fact-checking primary sources corrects inputs rather than the conclusion: FY28 consensus is $4.58, not $4.32; non-GAAP tax is ~7.5%, not 13%; the right share base is 575M including the mandatory convertible; and net debt is $5.09B, falling only ~$250-300M a quarter after dividends. With GM guided flat at 66-67% into December and distributor inventory lean at 25 days, near-term cycle risk is a bit lower than the bear weights imply. I nudge the median up to ~$84.5 and set fair value at $85, about 8% above spot plus a ~2.3% dividend. The main risks are an upcycle peaking around mid-2027 and the semiconductor sector multiple. The next test is Q2 FY27 earnings, expected around 2026-11-05 (not yet confirmed).

disagreements.topic: Diluted share count used in valuation
disagreements.resolution: Use 574-575M. Non-GAAP diluted shares were 574.3M in the June quarter (550.5M GAAP plus 23.8M from the 7.5% Series A mandatory convertible preferred) and are guided at 574.5-575.5M for the September quarter. The preferred converts automatically on 2028-03-15 into 16.006-19.608 shares per $1,000 (the minimum above $62.48 per share), so the 23.8M shares are certain. Dividing company-level FCF (before the ~$111M/yr preferred dividend) by 550M overstates value per share by about 4%.

disagreements.topic: Net debt level and pace of paydown
disagreements.resolution: Net debt was $5.09B at 2026-06-30 ($5,361M long-term debt less $272M cash; commercial paper and the Feb-2027 convertible are refinanceable under the revolver). Net debt fell only ~$170M in the June quarter because ~$275M a quarter goes to common and preferred dividends. With FCF of ~$520-600M a quarter, paydown runs ~$250-300M a quarter, which puts net debt at ~$3.7-3.9B by Sep-2027. The CFO expects net debt/EBITDA below 2.5x at end-September. Buybacks stay paused ($1.56B authorization unused) until debt is reduced.

FY28 consensus is $4.58 (25 analysts, range $4.08-5.44) on revenue of $7.43B, up from $4.19 60 days ago (20 upward revisions and 1 downward in 30 days). FY27 consensus is $3.65. Microchip's non-GAAP tax rate is ~7.5% (Q1: $35.6M on ~$474M pretax; Q2 guide $42-44M), not 13%. My bottom-up: $7.43B revenue, 65% GM, ~39-40% operating margin, ~$180M interest and ~8% tax give $4.38-4.49 on 575M shares. Consensus is therefore achievable if GM holds near 66%, and a 5% haircut to ~$4.40-4.50 is reasonable cycle discipline. The $4.32 figure agent 2 used as consensus is stale.

disagreements.topic: Gross margin: peak or heading back to 65%?
disagreements.resolution: At Citi on 2026-09-09 the CFO said GM should stay roughly flat at 66-67% in the December quarter. The one-time boosts in the September quarter (100%-margin licensing and gains on repricing distributor inventory) are replaced by the full-quarter effect of the mid-Aug/early-Sep price increase and lower underutilization charges. The long-term through-cycle model is 65%. A fall to 60% within 12 months would need a real demand reversal; it is a legitimate bear case but not the base drift.

disagreements.topic: Channel inventory and cycle position (double-ordering risk)
disagreements.resolution: Distributor inventory was 25 days at June 30 (26 at March 31), near the low end of the 17-43-day range of the past decade. Company inventory days fell from 185 to 175. Management says it sees no double ordering and no significant restocking. Lead-time stretch is mainly at outsourced foundry/OSAT capacity squeezed by AI demand. The quarter was the sixth straight of above-seasonal growth, with a seventh guided. The channel risk is lower than the agents' 25% bear weight suggests for the next 2-3 quarters. The risk is larger in mid-2027, when an ~8-quarter upcycle would be maturing and the market will be pricing FY29.

Peer forward P/Es (Aug-2026): NXPI 15.2x, ON 23.7x, ADI 30.4x, TXN 32.5x (~28x more recently). MCHP was 23.7x on FY27 and is ~17.2x FY28 consensus at $78.69. The 18.5-19x mid-cycle range on NTM EPS at the horizon is defensible: more leverage and more cyclicality than TXN/ADI, similar auto/industrial mix to NXPI/ON. 21x on a haircut EPS (agent 2) roughly equals 19x on consensus, so the fair values converge.
